questions.q: What does a .gitignore entry actually do?
options: Deletes the matching files from disk
Encrypts the matching files
Hides the matching files from your code editor
Tells Git to skip matching files/folders so they never get staged or tracked in the first place
questions.explain: .gitignore lists patterns that tell git status and git add to skip matching files — it has no effect on the files themselves, only on whether Git tracks them.

questions.q: Why should .sfdx/ and .sf/ be excluded from a Salesforce DX project's Git tracking?
options: They are required by Salesforce to remain untracked by law
They contain the actual Apex source code
They hold local, machine-specific CLI state (like authenticated org connections) that is meaningless or wrong on a teammate's machine
Git cannot physically store XML files
questions.explain: These folders hold CLI state specific to the machine that generated them — committing them risks a teammate picking up stale, machine-specific configuration that doesn't match their own setup.

questions.q: What does .forceignore control, as distinct from .gitignore?
options: Which metadata the sf CLI excludes when retrieving from or deploying to an org, independent of what Git tracks
The same thing as .gitignore — they're interchangeable
Which branches can be force-pushed
Which users can push to a protected branch
questions.explain: .forceignore is specific to the sf CLI's retrieve/deploy operations — a file can still be tracked in Git while being excluded from what the CLI moves between the project and an org.

questions.q: A developer committed .sfdx/ before adding a .gitignore entry for it. Why does .sfdx/ keep appearing in new commits even after the .gitignore entry is added?
options: Because .gitignore entries only apply to files not already tracked — an already-committed path keeps being tracked until explicitly untracked
Because .gitignore files don't work with Salesforce projects
Because .sfdx/ is a protected system folder Git cannot ignore
Because the .gitignore file itself needs to be committed twice
questions.explain: Adding a .gitignore entry only prevents future staging of a path — Git keeps tracking something that was already committed before the rule existed, until it's explicitly untracked.
